condition: Postpartum pre-eclampsia presenting as epigastric pain
permutationLabel: Day 6 after delivery, normotensive in pregnancy
summary: 29-year-old woman 6 days after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery with severe headache, blurred vision and epigastric pain; BP 166/108, proteinuria 2+, platelets 138, ALT 64. Postpartum pre-eclampsia with severe features.

inputs.hpi: Six days after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery (BP normal throughout pregnancy). Since yesterday: epigastric pain, severe frontal headache not relieved by paracetamol, blurred vision, nausea. Breastfeeding. Seen at a health centre and given antacids.

exam.general: BP 166/108, repeated 162/106. HR 88. Mild facial oedema.
exam.neuro: Brisk reflexes, no clonus, no focal deficit.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Postpartum pre-eclampsia with severe features (day 6)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Postpartum pre-eclampsia with severe features (BP 166/108, headache, visual disturbance, epigastric pain, proteinuria). Urgent obstetric review; antihypertensive (enalapril / nifedipine / labetalol, compatible with breastfeeding); consider magnesium sulfate.

mustInclude.note: Consider for postpartum pre-eclampsia with severe features / neurological symptoms.

mustExclude.note: No biliary disease: cholecystectomy would be a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: NICE NG133 — hypertension in pregnancy: diagnosis and management
guideline.section: Pre-eclampsia with severe hypertension or features (e.g. severe headache, visual disturbance, epigastric/RUQ pain, low platelets, raised transaminases, HELLP): admit under obstetric care; antihypertensives labetalol, nifedipine or methyldopa (ACE inhibitors and ARBs are not used in pregnancy); IV magnesium sulfate in severe pre-eclampsia when birth is planned or eclampsia is a concern; postnatal pre-eclampsia is managed with enalapril, nifedipine/amlodipine or labetalol
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Hypertension in pregnancy: diagnosis and management. NICE guideline NG133, 2019 (updated 2023).

guideline.name: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222 — gestational hypertension and preeclampsia
guideline.section: Severe features: SBP ≥ 160 or DBP ≥ 110, platelets < 100 × 10⁹/L, transaminases twice normal or severe persistent RUQ/epigastric pain, new cerebral or visual disturbance; HELLP syndrome; magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis; acute-onset severe hypertension treated urgently (labetalol, hydralazine, nifedipine); delivery at ≥ 34 weeks with severe features or HELLP; postpartum preeclampsia may present up to 6 weeks after birth
guideline.citation: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. Gestational hypertension and preeclampsia: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222. Obstet Gynecol. 2020;135:e237–e260.

rationale: Pre-eclampsia can first appear after delivery (up to 6 weeks). Once the patient is no longer pregnant, engines keyed on "pregnancy" lose the context; epigastric pain with headache, visual disturbance and severe hypertension must still be recognised.
